items.item_text: resume

Must possess valid California Driver's License to drive a County or University vehicle. Ability and means to travel on a flexible schedule as needed, proof of liability damage insurance on vehicle used is required. Reimbursement of job-related travel will be reimbursed according to University policies.
High school diploma or equivalent experience.

Reporting to the Director of Events Management, the Administrative Assistant provides administrative, fiscal, office, facility, and virtual meeting support for the entire Program Support Unit. The incumbent serves as the department's primary service desk operator, processes business documents, maintains office and equipment operations, manages room reservations, and provides Zoom meeting support. This position also provides occasional in-person event assistance as operational needs require.
Administrative support and department service desk:

Meticulous attention to detail and proactive follow-through are central to this role. Following training, the incumbent independently completes assigned routine to moderately complex work, tracks deadlines and outstanding items, and follows up with the director and others to keep work moving.

Monitor the department’s shared email inbox and general telephone line; respond promptly and professionally to standard questions about services, procedures, room reservations, equipment rentals, and meeting support.
This position is a career appointment that is 100% fixed.

Serve as a welcoming first point of contact for staff, clients, visitors, and partners. Clarify requests, provide accurate general information, and route specialized inquiries to the appropriate team member.
This position requires regular on-site work at the designated office in Davis, CA. Candidates must be available to work on-site as required to support business operations.

Track incoming requests, deadlines, outstanding questions, and follow-up actions; proactively request needed information or decisions from the director, team members, clients, and vendors. Monitor each item through completion, provide timely status updates, and flag delays before deadlines are missed.
Pay Scale: $30.87/hour to $36.24/hour
Maintain departmental records, shared files, contact information, calendars, forms, standard correspondence, and administrative trackers, including data in Airtable or other departmental systems.
This job is open until filled. The first application review date will be 12/2/2026.

Propose, develop, and implement practical administrative organization systems and workflow improvements in consultation with the director, including shared filing structures, request trackers, templates, and standard procedures. Translate approved ideas into usable tools, maintain them consistently, and help team members adopt them.
Coordinate routine internal scheduling, meeting materials, and administrative communications as assigned. Maintain current instructions and reference materials for recurring department services.
Independently resolve standard administrative matters within established procedures and refer unusual, confusing, or sensitive situations to the director or appropriate resource.
Business document processing and reconciliation:

Prepare, check for accuracy and completeness, process, and route purchasing requests, requisitions, purchase order documentation, check requests, interdepartmental order/charge documents (IOCs), vendor invoices, and other business transactions for the entire PSU team in accordance with established University procedures.

Prepare and submit travel reimbursements, expense reports, and purchasing-card reconciliation documentation; review receipts, chart of accounts information, and supporting materials for completeness and accuracy, and obtain missing information.

Prepare client invoices and departmental recharge documentation; track payments, outstanding balances, and transaction status, and follow up with clients, vendors, and appropriate business service units on routine issues.

Compare recorded expenses and routine ledger activity with supporting documentation and approved event or departmental budgets; identify discrepancies, coordinate corrections, and maintain expenditure and reconciliation trackers.
Prepare and route administrative documentation for contracts and service agreements; track required approvals, signatures, deadlines, and status without exercising signing authority.

Maintain accurate, organized fiscal and transaction records in accordance with established confidentiality, access, and retention procedures. Provide documentation and routine status reports to support event closeout, financial review, and audit requests.
Apply established purchasing, payment, and travel procedures; resolve routine processing questions and refer exceptions or requests requiring approval to the appropriate authority.
UC ANR conference room management (Davis Location):
Manage reservation requests and calendars for the UC ANR Conference Rooms, independently confirming routine bookings in accordance with established availability, capacity, access, and use procedures.
Review requests for completeness, scheduling conflicts, setup needs, and appropriate turnaround time. Resolve standard booking issues and refer unusual or unclear requests to the director.

Send confirmations and clear instructions covering room access, approved use, setup, available technology, cleanup, and responsibilities of the meeting organizer. Confirm required arrangements for any approved use outside regular office hours.
Coordinate and assist with room setup and basic audiovisual preparation; provide routine assistance to room users and coordinate additional support as needed.
Check rooms following use, identify needed resets, cleaning, repairs, or equipment follow-up, and coordinate resolution with users and appropriate support staff.
Maintain current room-use guidance, booking records, and reservation communications across departmental systems and calendars.
Office and equipment management:
Monitor and replenish office and event supplies; coordinate routine purchasing, deliveries, and inventory records, and identify cost-effective sources within established procurement procedures.
Organize and maintain departmental storage areas, supplies, and equipment so materials are accessible, accounted for, and stored safely.
Administer the department’s equipment rental program, including availability calendars, requests, checkout and return records, user instructions, and coordination of applicable rental charges.
Check equipment condition before checkout and after return; document missing items or damage, follow up with borrowers, and coordinate repairs or replacement through appropriate channels.
Provide basic equipment-use guidance within training and refer technical problems to the appropriate resource. Track equipment needs and report inventory or service concerns to the director.
Coordinate routine office service and maintenance requests with facilities, information technology, and other support units as needed.
Create and configure Zoom meetings, webinars, and registration pages using approved settings; prepare and distribute joining instructions and related communications.
Provide live virtual meeting support, including participant access, host/co-host controls, screen sharing, breakout rooms, chat, Q&A, and basic audio/video troubleshooting as assigned.
Conduct basic pre-meeting technology checks and help presenters and participants use the platform. Refer issues beyond training or access to the appropriate technical resource.
Manage authorized meeting recordings, recording access, registration data, and attendance reports in accordance with established procedures and privacy requirements.
In-person event backup and other assigned duties:

Provide occasional backup assistance for in-person meetings and events, including registration, materials preparation, room setup, participant assistance, and basic logistical support under the direction of the assigned event lead.
Complete other administrative and operational support duties within the scope of the classification.

Knowledge of office administration, routine purchasing and financial processing, recordkeeping, and expense reconciliation sufficient to review documentation and maintain accurate transaction records.

Exceptional attention to detail and consistent follow-through; ability to verify accuracy and completeness, track deadlines and outstanding items, proactively obtain needed information, and complete assignments without repeated reminders.
Ability to independently complete routine to moderately complex assignments after training, apply established procedures, exercise sound judgment, and recognize matters requiring escalation.

Clear oral and written communication skills, including the ability to explain procedures, prepare professional correspondence, and provide responsive service to people with varied backgrounds and needs.
Proficiency with Microsoft Outlook, Word, and Excel, including maintaining calendars, documents, spreadsheets, and routine financial or inventory trackers.
Ability to configure and support virtual meetings, troubleshoot basic participant issues, and learn Zoom features used by the department.
Ability to learn and accurately use UC and UC ANR policies, administrative systems, and departmental tools, including Airtable.
Ability to handle confidential fiscal, client, and participant information with discretion and maintain appropriate access to records.
Ability to work collaboratively with event staff, clients, vendors, and University service units while taking responsibility for assigned work.
Experience providing administrative or business operations support in a university, public agency, or comparable service environment.
Experience with UC or UC ANR purchasing, reimbursement, financial, and administrative procedures and systems, such as AggieEnterprise, AggieExpense, or successor systems.
Experience using Airtable or similar databases to maintain requests, operational records, and workflow trackers.
Experience providing live Zoom meeting or webinar support, including registration, recordings, participant management, and reporting.
Experience coordinating shared room reservations, equipment checkout, or office inventory.

Demonstrated interest and skill in organizing information and administrative workflows; ability to turn ideas into practical systems, document procedures, and sustain accurate, consistent system maintenance.
Special Conditions of Employment:

As of January 1, 2014, ANR is a smoke- and tobacco-free environment in which smoking, the use of smokeless tobacco products, and the use of unregulated nicotine products (e-cigarettes), is strictly prohibited.

“Misconduct” means any violation of the policies governing employee conduct at the applicant’s previous place of employment, including, but not limited to, violations of policies prohibiting sexual harassment, sexual assault, or other forms of harassment, or discrimination, as defined by the employer. For reference, below are UC’s policies addressing some forms of misconduct:
UC Sexual Violence and Sexual Harassment Policy
UC Anti-Discrimination Policy
Abusive Conduct in the Workplace
It is the policy of the University of California to undertake affirmative action and anti-discrimination efforts, consistent with its obligations as a Federal and State contractor.

The University reserves the right to make employment contingent upon successful completion of the background check. This is a designated position requiring a background check and may require fingerprinting due to the nature of the job responsibilities. UC ANR does hire people with conviction histories and reviews information received in the context of the job responsibilities.

As a condition of employment, you will be required to comply with the University of California Policy on Vaccination Programs, as may be amended or revised from time to time.  Federal, state, or local public health directives may impose additional requirements.

Misconduct Disclosure Requirement: As a condition of employment, the final candidate who accepts an offer of employment will be required to disclose if they have been subject to any final administrative or judicial decisions within the last seven years determining that they committed any misconduct; or have filed an appeal of a finding of substantiated misconduct with a previous employer.
